description: The repository shall maintain this catalog as the canonical record of Constellation requirements, ownership, implementation evidence, verification, milestones, release scope, sources, and known limitations.
notes: The schema preserves the common Taskyon and Syncpeer columns and adds Taskyon compatibility, milestone, and target-release tracking.

description: A requirement shall not be marked tracked or implemented until its owning implementation path and focused verification evidence are recorded.
notes: Existing Taskyon or Syncpeer behavior is dependency evidence, not Constellation implementation evidence.

description: Every requirement shall classify its relationship to Taskyon as native protocol reuse, layered application behavior, a runtime adapter, or local Constellation behavior.
notes: Allowed values are native, layered, adapter, and local.

description: Requirements shall use foundation, web-preview, 0.1, 0.2, post-1.0, or future milestones to express implementation order independently from release scope.
notes: A 0.1 requirement may have a foundation or web-preview milestone because target_release defines product inclusion.

description: Every requirement shall use target_release 0.1, 0.2, post-1.0, or future so the first usable release and its planned group-cache successor can be filtered without duplicating the catalog.
notes: Milestone orders implementation; target_release defines product scope. Later friend-network and stranger-cache versions remain future candidates, not committed release numbers.

description: Release 0.1 shall contain the complete first usable product scope; compatible 0.x releases may harden that scope from field evidence, and the same product shall become 1.0 only after satisfactory real-world browser, Android, relay, privacy, battery, and adverse-network validation.
notes: Version 1.0 is a maturity promotion rather than a smaller or separate feature set. Sensor, location, share, and transport wire versions evolve independently from product release numbers.

description: Release 0.1 shall ship the hosted browser app, an installable Tauri Android app, and installable Linux desktop artifacts consisting of an AppImage and a Flathub-ready Flatpak, and shall let two real people use independently generated links to share live locations in either direction across the supported clients, observe freshness and connected viewers, and stop or revoke access without developer tooling.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop local relay source/viewer reload and independent links;prior-revision Android managed API 29/API 36 flows;current APK build;nix run .#build-desktop-release-appimage and extracted AppImage launch smoke
notes: Browser local-relay sharing, independent links, and reload recovery have current evidence. Prior-revision Android Activity-home service sharing passed, but the current APK could not create a relay-reachable share in its managed API 36 run. The AppImage payload survived an extracted virtual-display smoke, not a host launcher check. Native multi-link identity/recovery, delegation/groups, Flatpak publication, hosted deployment, signed release, and physical-device acceptance remain required.

description: Constellation shall be distributed under the MIT License with copyright held by Xyntopia.
verification: LICENSE text;package metadata;nix develop --command yarn build:android:debug:x86_64-emulator
notes: The MIT license applies to Constellation source and metadata. Taskyon snapshots and map/software dependencies retain separate notices; the Linux secret-service crate is MIT OR Apache-2.0. A complete transitive license inventory for the shipped APK, AppImage, and Flatpak remains a publication gate.

description: Constellation shall consume versioned Taskyon packages only for shared protocol, P2P, Space, and generic map capabilities; Constellation-owned location behavior shall remain local and the repository shall never import sibling source paths or build artifacts.
notes: Until matching packages are published, Constellation vendors complete provenance-recorded snapshots of @taskyon/protocol and @taskyon/p2p-core as workspace packages. Generic changes are made in Taskyon first and synchronized; released package dependencies replace these snapshots later.

description: Constellation shall use pinned Taskyon-owned TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Vite configuration through a supported shared package.
notes: The self-contained 0.1 repository pins local configuration aligned with Taskyon and enforces formatting, lint, unit and static Android tests, and the production build in CI. Playwright and the Android harness remove inherited LD_LIBRARY_PATH before launching downloaded Chromium; scripts/browser-environment.test.mjs verifies this Nix host/browser boundary. A published Taskyon-owned configuration package remains required to establish one upstream owner and eliminate copied configuration drift.

description: Taskyon shall expose generic MapLibre and PMTiles behavior through a reusable package that does not require the complete Taskyon UI graph or contain location-domain semantics; Taskyon-specific range caching shall remain available through an injected source adapter.
verification: Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre test;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre typecheck;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre build
notes: The generic package is implemented locally but is not published or installed by Constellation. Constellation currently owns its thin map integration and location overlays.

description: A fresh Constellation checkout shall install, test, and build without a Taskyon sibling checkout; future Taskyon integration shall use released package versions rather than workspace links or relative sibling imports.
verification: yarn install --immutable;yarn lint;yarn test;yarn build;yarn test:e2e
notes: Constellation is self-contained through complete vendored Taskyon package snapshots with recorded provenance and documents its standalone web, desktop, and Android workflows. Application code imports package names only; published versions will replace the workspace snapshots without changing imports.

description: Constellation shall supersede the unauthenticated in-memory Deno and SSE location prototype after equivalent basic live sharing is verified.
notes: The prototype remains a UX reference and is not a production compatibility contract.

description: Taskyon shall define a transport-independent read-only sensor service for dynamically described sensors and authenticated observations.
verification: Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol sensor client/server unit test;Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol type-check and build
notes: The versioned descriptor, observation, subscribe, unsubscribe, and event contract exists. Authentication, grants, advertisements, signatures, and peer transport integration remain planned; release 0.1 will expose only Constellation's location profile.

description: A peer shall declare zero or more stable sensor endpoints without requiring a centrally fixed list of sensor kinds.
notes: Declarations are descriptive and grant no authority by themselves.

description: Each sensor endpoint shall identify a versioned profile or canonical schema revision, value shape, units, quality metadata, stream behavior, and owning service principal.
notes: Release 0.1 interprets only the location profile and rejects unsupported required profiles without executing custom semantics.

description: The sensor model shall support interoperable Taskyon standard profiles and dynamically declared custom schemas through the same descriptor mechanism.
notes: Profile interpretation remains separate from transport and discovery.

description: Every observation shall bind its sensor identifier, descriptor revision, source principal, monotonic sequence, capture time, value payload, and quality metadata to an authenticated source envelope.
notes: Receivers reject invalid signatures, schemas, bounds, and replayed or regressing sequences.

description: Authorized consumers shall receive current and subsequent observations through one bounded Taskyon protocol stream with explicit cancellation and backpressure.
verification: yarn test:unit;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop two independent sources
notes: An authenticated stream per viewer has bounded framing and queues, subscribe/unsubscribe, heartbeat cleanup and transport close. A newly created share seeds its first observation from a still-fresh current fix, so a stationary source need not wait for another GPS event. Observations are not persisted.

description: A separately authorized sensor-history capability shall stream a bounded time range without exposing provider paths or an unbounded query surface.
notes: Constellation initially permits at most the latest 30 minutes for remote location views.

description: A signed expiring service advertisement shall identify protocol and descriptor revisions, routing information, limits, and expiry without revealing private Space membership.
notes: Advertisement proves neither authorization nor correct behavior.

description: Space or transient-share grants shall independently authorize publish-own and read-current operations for explicit sensors and bounded scopes.
notes: Read access never implies publication, history access, delegation, device control, or Space administration.

description: Writable attributes and device commands shall remain outside the first sensor protocol and require a separate future command capability and authorization review.
notes: A generic sensor declaration must not become an unrestricted remote-control surface.

description: Sensor endpoint, profile, attribute, and event concepts shall preserve a clean future mapping to Matter while making no initial Matter wire-compatibility claim.
source: Connectivity Standards Alliance Matter specification;Thread Group resources
notes: A Matter bridge will be a separately authorized and tested adapter.

description: Constellation shall treat libp2p as connectivity fabric and the Taskyon sensor protocol as the application layer rather than coupling sensor semantics to one network transport.
notes: This is architectural alignment, not Thread protocol implementation.

description: Constellation shall define a versioned location profile carried inside Taskyon's generic sensor observation payload, including source-owned disclosure precision, bounded coordinates, uncertainty, capture and expiry times, and optional altitude, heading, and speed.
notes: The validated application profile is local to Constellation so Taskyon does not acquire a product-specific location package. Mapping it into the generic Taskyon sensor envelope and peer authorization remain planned.

description: Location observations shall use source-owned monotonic sequences and explicit capture and expiry times so receivers can reject replay and display stale state honestly.
notes: The browser source emits monotonic sequence and explicit capture/expiry times; the viewer rejects non-increasing sequences and recomputes live, delayed, and stale map state. Wall-clock timestamps alone never establish authority.

description: A publishing device shall adapt sampling to movement, elapsed time, requested detail, power state, and a maximum interval through simple battery-versus-detail presets.
notes: Continuous maximum-rate GPS is not the default.

description: When an authorized viewer subscribes and the source's last fix is older than thirty seconds or absent, the source shall request one fresh location fix, rate-limited to one request per minute per device. The last known observation remains viewable as stale while the request is pending; movement-only background sampling remains the baseline.
verification: src/location/browser.test.ts;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop reconnect;nix develop --command yarn build:android:debug:x86_64-emulator;Android one-shot device acceptance pending
notes: A successful authenticated sensor subscription triggers a single current-position request only when the last fix is old. Android's foreground service selects the network provider when enabled, otherwise GPS; API 29 uses requestSingleUpdate. It times out after twenty seconds. Doze and provider availability can still delay or prevent an update; no guaranteed delivery time is claimed. The source restoration path also adopts an already acquired fresh GPS fix so a viewer need not wait for further movement.

description: The source shall choose exact, one-kilometre approximate, or city-sized very coarse disclosure independently for each active share and shall always see the active choice.
notes: New shares default to approximate, exact is explicit, and projection happens independently per share. The active list names very coarse separately. The third-choice mobile button and final action fit the Pixel 5 emulated viewport; native visual acceptance remains pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall offer a third source-selected sharing preset that publishes a stable city-sized uncertainty area of at least 20 km radius, without naming a city or changing the source's own map position. Its randomized center must scale with the selected radius rather than remaining within the one-kilometre mode's small offset; the transmitted location and redeem response remain approximate for older viewers.
verification: src/shareDraft.test.ts;src/location/approximation.test.ts;src/android/backgroundSharing.test.ts;tests/share-flow.spec.ts desktop and mobile;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop P2P broad-area delivery and browser reload;yarn typecheck;yarn test:android:config;nix develop --command yarn build:android:debug:x86_64-emulator
notes: The 20 km minimum uses radius-scaled random center placement and the existing per-share hysteresis and overlap; after a temporary poor-accuracy enlargement a new region can shrink toward the preset. Protected source settings survived browser reload in the focused relay test. P2P delivery through the unchanged approximate wire contract passed; the Android x86_64 debug APK compiled. Android on-device and physical-device sharing remain unverified. Adjustable radius is future UX work. City-sized areas reduce precision, not anonymity.

description: For each share using approximate precision, the source shall publish a soft circular uncertainty region with a default one-kilometre radius and keep that region stable while the reported position and its reported GPS uncertainty remain safely contained.
notes: Each in-memory share independently draws cryptographically secure random center and threshold values; there is no grid, reusable seed, share-secret derivation, or per-sample randomization.

description: The source shall create a new randomized uncertainty region only after crossing its private hysteresis threshold consistently, or earlier when needed to preserve containment; consecutive regions shall overlap by at least 75 percent of their area, and poor GPS accuracy shall enlarge the advertised radius rather than exclude the reported uncertainty.
notes: Two consecutive threshold crossings, immediate containment repair, overlap enlargement, and poor-accuracy enlargement are implemented. Browser region control state is encrypted and restored per link; restart behavior is covered by the browser relay test, but native region restoration and an explicit continuity test remain pending.

description: Approximate observations shall expose only the advertised region and freshness needed to render it; they shall not expose exact coordinates, grid identifiers, random inputs, private thresholds, speed, or heading.
notes: The published approximate payload contains only the randomized area center, containing radius, source sequence, and freshness timestamps; altitude, heading, speed, threshold, random inputs, and exact coordinates are omitted.

description: The UI and documentation shall state that approximate sharing reduces precision but does not provide anonymity or a formal privacy guarantee, and that long trajectories, known places, screenshots, copied observations, or colluding recipients can still reveal sensitive patterns.
notes: About now explains that neighborhood and city-sized areas reduce precision without making the source anonymous. The fuller threat list, including colluding recipients and screenshots, is still missing from the user-facing explanation. Received approximate locations remain areas without a center point.

description: A viewer shall distinguish live, delayed, stale, expired, revoked, and unavailable location state instead of silently presenting old coordinates as current.
notes: The most recent observation remains in memory across disconnect and reconnect until Stop following, and the map marks it stale. Show on map appears only after an observation exists. The details show last update time and age. Received coordinates are still not persisted across app restart; distinct expired/revoked presentation and native acceptance remain pending.

description: Constellation shall present one local person identity with independently named and revocable device identities, each of which may publish its own authorized location.
notes: A device identity does not independently grant broad access to user or Space data.

description: A new source or viewer shall receive a local device identity without registration, hosted account authentication, or disclosure of a stable identity to other link recipients.
notes: Deleting local application data may destroy the local identity and active shares; account recovery is outside 0.1.

description: Background publishers shall receive a narrow device-bound principal and publish-own grant without receiving Space administration or read access to unrelated sensors.
notes: This is the unattended-service boundary used while the phone is locked.

description: Missing membership, grant, publication, or distribution policy shall deny location access.
notes: Global discovery never advertises Space membership.

description: The initial UI shall expose shares and connections rather than requiring users to understand Space keys, overlays, grants, or service advertisements.
notes: Security mechanics remain inspectable in diagnostics and advanced details.

description: A future named family or friends group shall be an independent collaborative Space rather than an extension of the user's default personal Space.
notes: Location publication remains opt-in per Space.

description: Ordinary group members shall be able to publish their own location and view members who currently choose to share, while administrators alone manage membership.
notes: Joining a group never starts location sharing automatically.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support promotion and revocation of multiple administrators and explicit ownership transfer.
notes: Administration remains separate from ordinary membership and device control.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support an offline recovery secret without putting root keys or reusable administrator credentials in invitations, links, logs, or QR codes.
notes: Recovery requires bootstrap access to an authorized provider or rendezvous network.

description: Equivalent location data shared into different transient share scopes shall be encrypted independently to reduce provider-side correlation.
notes: Each live share projection is derived from the current source observation and encrypted for only its authorized scope; named Spaces inherit this rule after 1.0.

description: Persistent Space enrollment shall use short-lived single-use QR or invite links with out-of-band fingerprint confirmation and existing-administrator approval.
notes: This enrollment flow is distinct from pre-authorized transient location links.

description: A location link shall create a narrow encrypted share scope and read grant without enrolling receivers as people, devices, or members of a collaborative Space.
notes: A link grants only its source location sensor on authenticated per-viewer streams. Browser grants persist encrypted across reload; native encrypted recovery code now exists but is not runtime-verified. Named Space integration remains future work.

description: The share URL shall place the bearer capability in its fragment and shall not expose it to HTTP requests, referrers, logs, analytics, or messenger link-preview fetches.
notes: Fragment-only encoding and browser session-only redemption are implemented; the visible fragment is cleared after connection. Native viewers retain explicit acceptance. Deployed hosting and Android handoff remain unverified.

feature: Immediate browser view and optional keep
description: A browser visitor opening a valid share fragment shall see the sender's live location immediately without an acceptance modal or own-GPS request. The connection shall be session-only until Keep following persists it; the sender may observe viewer presence and connection metadata.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts browser preview and saved-follow reload;tests/share-flow.spec.ts invalid fragment;src/sharing/sharingRuntime.test.ts
notes: Immediate browser preview and optional encrypted save are implemented. The sender name is learned after redemption and never added to the URL; local nickname is not sent in redemption. Saving can begin own GPS but denial does not block saved following. A preview notice offers Stop preview; malformed links show a redacted error. Expired-link and mobile browser acceptance remain unverified.

description: Android shall accept valid Constellation HTTPS links through ACTION_VIEW and text/plain ACTION_SEND from apps such as Signal, while desktop Tauri shall route a pasted valid link directly to the approval flow. Native links require a View location tap before redemption, followed by editable nickname confirmation.
notes: Android ACTION_SEND text is consumed once and a valid URL from surrounding text enters native approval; ACTION_VIEW uses the existing deep-link adapter. Desktop paste enters the same approval flow. APK compiles but cold/warm intent delivery and hosted App Links are not runtime-verified; no in-app camera scanner is planned.

description: A compact transparent bottom control row shall show independent Sharing and Seeing list buttons around one plus expander, with subdued own-location and P2P status. Expanded Add location and Share location actions shall float above the row without a divider or resizing the map, and fold after a successful action while remaining reopenable with a remembered collapsed state.
verification: tests/map-ui.spec.ts selected desktop layout checks;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts source/share controls;mobile visual check pending
notes: The compact dock, subdued status, and remembered expander are implemented. Two prominent orange actions float above it; the dock has no panel background or top border, and opening actions does not resize the map. Narrow-screen and Android visual acceptance remain pending.

description: Constellation's on-screen iconography shall use small SVG controls rather than text glyphs or bitmap buttons. The upper-left menu and upper-right recenter button shall share one top row; recentering shall use a clearly visible filled Constellation star within a centering reticle.
verification: yarn typecheck;tests/map-ui.spec.ts selected desktop checks;mobile visual check pending
notes: Menu sits at the upper left and a filled orange Constellation star inside an outlined centering reticle sits at the upper right in the same row. QR codes and platform launcher assets remain separate. Mobile contrast and touch-target acceptance remain pending.

description: The location-sharing dialog shall keep its settings, selection buttons, and final share action visible together on common phone viewports without requiring vertical scrolling; unusually short viewports may scroll rather than clip controls.
verification: tests/share-flow.spec.ts Pixel 5 emulation final-action bounds;native visual check pending
notes: Three precision choices fit one compact row; the final action stays within the emulated mobile viewport. Native visual acceptance and unusually short viewport handling remain pending.

feature: Close menu after selection or outside click
description: Selecting any menu entry shall perform its action and close the menu, including when selecting the already active map style; clicking or tapping outside the menu shall close it even if the map cannot initialize.
verification: Browser Playwright smoke covered menu toggle, active style selection, working-map click, unavailable-WebGL map tap, and top-bar outside click;other entries pending
notes: The screen handles outside clicks before child controls process them. The menu button remains toggleable and menu items run their own actions; map clicks, map controls, and empty top-bar space all dismiss the menu without depending on a MapLibre click event.

description: A future explicit user setting may open Constellation HTTPS share links in the installed desktop app while preserving bearer-capability secrecy and a browser fallback.
notes: Ordinary desktop HTTPS clicks open the browser and desktop paste starts native approval in 0.1. Tauri Linux deep links pass URLs as process arguments, so do not route current secret-bearing fragments through a custom URI or claim automatic handoff yet.

description: The browser preview may offer compact Android Play Store, F-Droid, and GitHub release links after each destination is real and configured; absent destinations shall not render dead buttons or block viewing.
notes: No live store or release destination is currently configured. Install links are not required for account-free browser viewing in 0.1.

description: Android and Linux desktop shall restore saved followed links and peer identity from app-specific protected storage, using Android Keystore encryption and a Linux Secret Service item. Session previews shall remain usable when protected storage is unavailable but no plaintext persistence fallback is allowed.
verification: nix develop --command cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml;nix develop --command yarn build:android:debug:x86_64-emulator;src/sharing/sharingRuntime.test.ts
notes: Android UI state uses its own Keystore alias and preferences namespace, separate from clearable background-service status. Linux saves the protected record directly in Secret Service with no plaintext file fallback. When loading protected storage fails, previews are ephemeral and save is refused. Actual reload recovery on native devices and locked-keyring behavior remain unverified.

description: The web and Android apps shall use the system share surface so a source can send the generated URL through Signal or another installed messenger without messenger-specific account integration.
notes: The web app uses Web Share when available and clipboard copy otherwise. Android system-share verification remains pending.

description: A source shall choose duration, precision, and viewer capacity before generating a link so valid receivers need no later source approval.
notes: Duration, precision, capacity, HMAC redemption, whole-link stop, and automatic expiry are enforced. A per-session revocation control remains unimplemented.

description: A multi-recipient link shall expose only the source's authorized location; receivers shall not discover one another or gain reciprocal sharing automatically.
notes: Two people share in both directions in 0.1 by independently creating one-way links; receivers receive no peer list or reciprocal grant.

description: A source shall show a QR for its one-way fragment link. An external scanner shall open a browser preview immediately when the app is absent or enter explicit native acceptance when the Android app is installed; neither path creates collaborative Space membership.
notes: QR generation and browser immediate preview of its URL are implemented. No in-app scanning library is required now; hosted web deployment and verified Android App Links remain prerequisites for seamless external scanning. Reciprocal pairing remains separate.

description: Sharing shall default to one hour, offer longer presets including eight hours, and stop publication and retrieval automatically at expiry.
notes: The source rejects expired redemption and heartbeat operations, closes expired sessions, and removes expired in-memory shares.

description: An until-revoked link shall exist only as an advanced option behind a prominent warning and explicit source confirmation.
notes: The UI requires fresh acknowledgement and offers whole-link stop. Browser grants now survive reload, increasing the importance of conspicuous active-share status. Native recovery and long-running revocation verification remain pending.

description: A source shall select a viewer capacity with quick choices of one, ten, and fifty plus an advanced no-share-level-cap option.
notes: Admission enforces the chosen capacity; no-share-level-cap still has a hard runtime ceiling of 128 active sessions.

description: Each successful link redemption shall create a separate ephemeral viewer session so forwarding and concurrent use can be counted, bounded, and revoked.
notes: Each stream gets a nonce-bound HMAC redemption and random in-memory session identifier. Whole-share revocation now flushes its terminal event before transport close, and the viewer marks the follow disconnected; individual session UI remains pending.

description: Viewer sessions shall send bounded heartbeats so the source can see connected-session counts and expand each share link into short per-link peer fingerprints, last-seen freshness, and private editable device labels without claiming verified human identity.
verification: src/sharing/shareProtocol.test.ts;tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop source/viewer flow and label recovery
notes: Connected-session counting, 35-second heartbeat cleanup, and per-link hashed peer fingerprints are implemented. Editable device labels are stored only in protected local state and never sent by the viewer; a forwarded link and fingerprint do not verify a person. Per-session revocation, disconnected-device management, and Android visual acceptance remain pending.

description: The source shall be able to revoke one viewer session without revoking every receiver using the same link.
notes: Revocation prevents future access but cannot erase already observed information.

description: The product shall describe active viewers as connected Constellation sessions and shall not claim to count screenshots, copied coordinates, modified clients, or downstream rebroadcasts.
notes: The UI labels the number as connected sessions. It is operational presence, not proof of human attention or non-retention.

description: Two devices shall establish reciprocal view grants through a hidden pair scope after both people independently confirm their own duration and precision.
notes: Stopping or expiring one direction does not silently stop or extend the other direction.

description: The map screen and Android notification shall continuously show whether sharing is active, its recipients or scope, precision, expiry, and a one-action stop control.
notes: The map shows active share and connected-session counts. The active-share sheet reopens each link or QR and revokes it independently. Per-session stop, expiration details in the compact status, and notification-action verification remain pending.

description: Release 0.1 clients and providers shall not persist exact or approximate location observations; an already connected viewer may retain only its latest observation in memory and shall mark it stale when the source becomes unavailable.
notes: Browser persistence contains grants and approximation control state but no observations. Android service now keeps full location status only in process memory and redacts the observation before encrypting the durable status. Device-level inspection and process-recreation evidence are still needed. Durable self-history and hosted last-known state are deferred.

description: Remote trail access shall expose only bounded viewing streams with no export operation or persistent viewer cache while acknowledging that an authorized viewer can capture rendered data.
notes: The protocol shall not make an unenforceable DRM claim.

description: A device's durable trail shall contain only samples generated by that device and shall never append locations received from another peer.
notes: This prevents ordinary viewers from becoming accidental history replicas or onward publishers.

description: A device shall append self-generated samples to bounded daily text journals containing a versioned header and one authenticated base64url ciphertext envelope per line.
notes: No database is required; plaintext coordinates never enter the journal.

description: Journal envelopes shall authenticate device identity, format version, sequence, capture time, and previous-envelope commitment so truncation, reordering, replay, and corruption are detected.
notes: Recovery may preserve valid prefixes while reporting damaged or missing suffixes.

description: Completed daily or size-bounded journals shall rotate into signed immutable segments suitable for verification and optional blind replication.
notes: Mutable current journals remain local and have one owning writer.

description: Self-history shall default to thirty days and offer shorter periods or keep-until-deleted; cleanup shall remove complete expired segments and their keys or envelopes.
notes: Retention changes do not silently publish or replicate history.

description: Android shall protect the local trail key with Android Keystore so an explicitly started background share can continue after screen lock without exposing a broad Space or user root key.
notes: Behavior after reboot follows platform protected-data availability and fails closed when the key is unavailable.

description: A source shall derive the minimum authorized time range from local self-history and encrypt a separate projection for each Space or transient share scope.
notes: Canonical self-history is never handed directly to a remote provider.

description: Selected storage services may retain opaque source-authored immutable trail segments without receiving plaintext, Space membership, or decryption authority.
notes: Ordinary viewer devices do not satisfy replica durability targets.

description: A source may grant remote viewers access to at most the latest thirty minutes of its trail through a bounded memory-only stream.
notes: The viewer discards the window on close, expiry, or revocation.

description: Official clients shall not write another device's received trail to persistent storage or re-advertise it as a local sensor history.
notes: A malicious authorized client can still capture plaintext and is outside this enforceable guarantee.

description: The web app shall use Taskyon browser libp2p with WebRTC, WebTransport, secure WebSockets, and circuit-relay transport as available.
notes: The browser runtime reserves configured relay reachability, advertises addresses only inside the bearer fragment, and opens one Noise-protected protocol stream per viewer. Transport-specific status detail remains limited.

description: Taskyon P2P shall provide a js-libp2p transport adapter backed by Tauri native sockets so Android is not limited to browser WebRTC connectivity.
notes: The adapter belongs upstream in Taskyon and must preserve the same peer identity and stream semantics.

feature: Native HTTP and secure relay access
description: The Android host shall expose bounded native HTTP or secure WebSocket connectivity needed for bootstrap, relay, and provider access without exposing generic unrestricted network calls to the UI.
notes: Native networking is capability-scoped and uses the same service contracts as web transports.

description: Peers shall try compatible direct transports first and then configured Taskyon circuit relays and gateways with bounded retries and backoff.
notes: The viewer orders non-circuit addresses before circuit addresses and the source tries configured relays. Source reachability is checked against the actual connected relay address. A failed startup stops its unreachable peer. Viewer reconnect retains its last observation while seeking a new authenticated one, but the retry sweep is still ten seconds and adverse-network behavior is not verified. Hosted-relay Android reachability, timed backoff, and controlled direct-path diagnostics remain pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall operate production bootstrap, rendezvous, secure WebSocket or WebTransport, and circuit-relay endpoints separately from the static web app so browser and Android peers can connect when direct paths fail.
verification: 2026-09-24 live Chromium startPrivateBrowserPeer reservation returned one reachable address
notes: A previous browser probe received RESERVATION_REFUSED, but a fresh browser-runtime probe successfully reserved a hosted relay address; a Node-only listener probe was invalid because that node lacks the relay listener transport. Android still reported no relay-reachable address in an earlier managed run; no current cross-device or multi-network acceptance is available. The Taskyon-operated service cannot guarantee networks that block every outbound path.

description: A Space or advanced user shall be able to configure additional bootstrap, relay, and blind-storage providers without replacing the Taskyon protocol.
notes: Provider selection remains separate from service advertisement and authorization.

description: Share and Space traffic shall use cryptographically separate overlays whose identifiers, grants, and contents are absent from global discovery.
notes: Release 0.1 quick shares avoid stable secret-derived discovery tokens and carry reachability plus independent random grant secrets in URL fragments. Full private Taskyon rendezvous remains planned.

description: Hosted relays, mesh routers and Space bridges shall forward opaque end-to-end encrypted traffic without receiving location plaintext, reusable share capabilities, or implicit collaborative Space membership.
notes: A router that decrypts or republishes data is a distinct service principal requiring an explicit grant; ordinary routing never grants sensor access.

description: In release 0.2 a publisher may explicitly allow opted-in devices in a quick-share group to cache only its latest application-encrypted observation per rotating opaque mailbox, for at most 24 hours and never beyond the share expiry. A cache grant never grants location-viewing authority.
notes: Release 0.1 remains memory-only and live P2P. Group sharing is a prerequisite; named Taskyon Spaces are not required for this first group cache. The one-minute freshness expiry and longer last-known retention are distinct; receivers label older observations stale. Ordinary peers have a default capacity of 100 different share mailboxes, not 100 samples per source. Cached plaintext and reusable share capabilities are forbidden. Revocation cannot erase plaintext previously viewed and deletion notices may arrive late.

description: The first relevant group-sharing flow shall ask each publisher whether its own share may use encrypted last-known caching; caching is off by default and each potential storage device separately opts in to host cache duty. The prompt shall explain 24-hour maximum retention, source expiry, and connection-metadata visibility without claiming anonymity.
notes: One group member's cache consent never enables caching for another member's publication. A group cache may be a member without being permitted to view a hub-mode location.

description: Opted-in reachable group devices shall rotate the active cache role through bounded leases with an acknowledged overlapping handoff, favoring charging devices while balancing extra duty over time. No cache volunteer or interrupted handoff shall degrade ordinary live sharing or be represented as a guaranteed always-online service.
notes: The role rotates cache availability work, not all battery use from location acquisition or P2P presence. Duplicate ciphertext during handoff is deduplicated by authenticated source ordering; every provider applies bounded quotas and expiry.

description: Viewing, publishing, caching ciphertext, relaying, delegating, and group administration shall be separate grants. Direct peers, quick-share groups, delegated peers, friends of friends, and strangers discovered globally have progressively weaker relationship trust but no implicit authority from their tier alone.
notes: Release 0.2 only enables explicitly opted-in group caches. A later version may let one device cache for several separate friend networks with isolated keys, mailboxes, quotas, and grants; unrelated networks must not learn one another's membership. Stranger caching requires explicit admission and abuse controls, not a reputation score based on self-reported capacity.

description: After less-trusted caching is safe, an optional headless Constellation peer may join the same blind-cache protocol with a configured capacity up to 100000 latest share mailboxes, without becoming a special trusted server or gaining location-viewing authority.
notes: This is not required for 0.2. Packaging, durable storage, quotas, and abuse resistance remain deployment work even though the wire protocol is shared with ordinary cache peers.

description: The product shall not promise connectivity through total network loss, captive portals, or networks that block every available outbound transport.
notes: Diagnostics identify direct, relayed, offline, blocked, and degraded states.

description: Relays and publishers shall enforce bounded messages, stream counts, heartbeats, quotas, rates, and expiries before allocating unbounded work.
notes: Client frames are limited to 8192 bytes and 32 pending messages, links to four addresses and 1800 fragment characters, sessions to 128, remembered redemption nonces to 1024 per share, and heartbeat/expiry cleanup is bounded. Hosted relay quotas require separate deployment evidence.

description: Future Constellation viewer sessions shall operate unchanged over Taskyon logical streams routed across multiple peer links while preserving per-viewer authorization, counting, expiry, revocation, ordering and explicit route-failure state.
notes: Intermediate routing belongs to Taskyon P2P beneath the sensor protocol. This is not part of release 0.1.

description: Future location sessions shall be able to traverse mixed LAN, Bluetooth, WebRTC, native-socket and relay links without introducing transport-specific location messages or weakening authorization.
notes: Bluetooth and LAN are planned link adapters, not currently implemented transports or claims of Thread, Zigbee or Bluetooth Mesh wire compatibility.

description: A future reachable LAN or mesh gateway shall be able to carry multiplexed upstream traffic and route separate encrypted viewer sessions to several authorized downstream peers without becoming a location viewer by default.
notes: The source retains per-viewer capacity, presence and revocation semantics. Plaintext redistribution requires a separate explicit service grant.

description: Future mesh routing may retain only the newest bounded encrypted location frame across intermittent links and shall discard it at the source-controlled expiry without constructing a trail or durable received-location history.
notes: Blind routers receive no location plaintext. Longer queues and history remain separate capabilities.

description: A future opt-in mode shall let an authorized device carry bounded end-to-end-encrypted latest-location records across disconnected Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi groups, synchronize by authenticated inventory and deduplicate by source-scoped opaque record ID and sequence, then forward eligible records on reconnection to another local mesh or the Internet.
notes: A hiking group may exchange encrypted last-known positions across short-range hops; a member who leaves can carry eligible records to another group kilometres away. This is asynchronous ferrying, not a guaranteed 500 m Bluetooth link or real-time mesh. Source-controlled expiry, bounded storage, quotas, revocation checks when reachable, freshness labels, and loop/duplicate suppression still apply. Longer retention or trails require a separate explicit grant; the ordinary 0.2 cache remains latest-only and capped at 24 hours. An offline-only transport choice must not silently upload on Internet reconnection.

description: Cross-group forwarding and viewing shall be independently authorized: a carrier may copy opaque records only under a source or group forwarding grant, and members of a newly encountered group may decrypt them only under pre-authorized read or explicitly delegated emergency-view grants with bounded sources, recipients, precision and expiry.
notes: Merely meeting another group must never make the original group's positions readable. If the injured source cannot grant access while offline, the necessary emergency read/delegation policy must already exist; exact policy and consent UI require a separate threat-model decision. Metadata visible to carriers and recipients must be documented. No life-safety delivery claim without field validation.

description: Future native clients shall offer explicit Bluetooth-only and local Wi-Fi-only sharing modes as well as automatic transport selection, carrying the same authenticated Taskyon logical messages and encrypted cache records without requiring cellular or Internet connectivity.
notes: Local Wi-Fi includes LAN and device-to-device options where supported. Strict offline modes must not fall back to cellular, Internet relays, or later upload without an explicit policy change. Discovery, pairing, MTU, permissions, Android background limits, battery cost, supported hardware, and multi-hop routing require device-level validation. No claim of Bluetooth Mesh interoperability follows from using Bluetooth links.

description: The transport-independent mesh envelope may later support explicit external long-range radio adapters such as LoRa or other locally permitted sub-GHz hardware for low-rate store-and-forward traffic, without changing location, chat, or authorization semantics.
notes: No specific band, range, throughput, or off-the-shelf phone support is promised. Fragmentation, replay protection, power use, device support, and regional spectrum and duty-cycle rules require a separate design and field review before implementation.

description: Future routing and caching shall maintain local, decaying, role-specific reliability scores from directly observed delivery, availability, and protocol behavior; cryptographically demonstrable invalid messages or grant violations may trigger immediate local quarantine, while mere silence or poor radio links affect route preference rather than proving malice.
notes: Do not accept self-reported capacity or unverified accusations as reputation evidence, or publish a global blacklist. Bound scoring by identity/role, resist churn and Sybil abuse with admission and quotas, allow decay and recovery, and keep alternative routes and redundant cache holders so excluding one peer does not partition the group. No scoring system can reliably distinguish intentional packet loss from an intermittent link or guarantee quick global removal of an attacker.

feature: Optional Tor connectivity and anonymity study
description: Evaluate an optional Tor-routed Internet transport for native or headless Taskyon/Constellation peers and onion-hosted bootstrap or relay endpoints, with a strict privacy mode that prevents direct-path and ancillary-network fallbacks before promising anonymity.
notes: Tor requires Internet and cannot replace disconnected Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi links. Browser WebRTC, DNS, bootstrap, map-tile requests and other direct traffic can reveal IP or link activity; simply adding a Tor proxy to the current browser app is not an anonymity guarantee. Evaluate metadata, identity/link correlation, timing, latency, Android integration, and failure behavior before choosing an implementation; end-to-end encryption remains necessary.

description: A future Constellation chat shall use Taskyon's versioned messaging contracts, FRP streams and libp2p logical network to exchange authenticated end-to-end-encrypted one-to-one and group messages over direct, relayed and permitted offline transports, with separately consented bounded store-and-forward delivery.
notes: Taskyon's current diagnostic P2P chat is not a production encrypted offline messenger. Generic message/envelope semantics belong upstream in Taskyon; Constellation keeps its UI and policy local. Chat needs per-conversation bounded message queues, expiry, deduplication, ordering and delivery state, not the latest-location-only cache; separate cache and read grants and metadata limits apply. Offline delivery is best-effort until field validated.

description: Future synthetic tests shall exercise Bluetooth-only and Wi-Fi-only isolation, disconnected cache-carrier handoff, cross-group read and forward grants, expiry and revocation during outages, peer quarantine and recovery, route diversity, and chat delivery without plaintext at blind caches.

description: The browser shall persist its own peer identity, active grants, approximate-region control state, followed links, local follow-start timestamps, and private viewer-device labels in authenticated encrypted local storage without storing received location observations.
notes: IndexedDB stores AES-GCM ciphertext with a non-extractable WebCrypto key in the same browser profile. Viewer last-known coordinates remain in memory only. Restored source shares now adopt an already acquired fresh fix, closing a startup race that left viewers connected but waiting until the next GPS callback. A ten-second retry sweep reconnects viewers. This protects against casual storage inspection, not a malicious same-origin script or profile owner; concurrent tabs and storage eviction remain pending.

description: Desktop and Android shall protect and restore peer keys, grants, follow metadata, and approximate-region state using platform-secured storage without silently changing share identity after restart.
notes: Browser IndexedDB recovery is not an adequate native secure-store design. Android service currently stores the request but fails closed on process death because the peer key is not restored; desktop/Android UI links are ephemeral.

description: The menu shall offer Protomaps light/dark as Default and grayscale/black as Minimalist, follow the system color scheme, preserve the chosen family and map camera across style switches, and use local device fonts for labels without bundled glyph ranges.
verification: tests/map-ui.spec.ts desktop and mobile;browser style-and-tile smoke;yarn typecheck
notes: Styles use the existing Taskyon PMTiles archive and locally bundled sprites. Omitting the glyph URL makes MapLibre GL JS generate labels from local device fonts; appearance and script coverage vary by device. Desktop WebKit archive fetching and native label appearance still need visual verification; there is no third-party tile fallback or offline range cache.

description: The map shall visibly credit its map-data providers in small unobtrusive text at the lower-right edge, clear of the primary sharing button. The About surface shall ship map, sprite, and upstream-code notices for redistributable artifacts and explain that map labels use device fonts.
verification: tests/map-ui.spec.ts desktop selected checks;Protomaps and Tangram upstream license comparison
source: OpenStreetMap copyright;Protomaps basemaps licenses;Protomaps basemaps-assets;Tangram icons MIT license;Overture Maps attribution
notes: OSM, Protomaps and ESA credit is shown even when PMTiles loading fails; it sits at the map viewport's lower-right corner above the separate action dock without a bordered panel. The bundled notice separates Protomaps BSD-3-Clause code and CC0 visual design from Tangram-derived MIT sprite icons, preserves the exact 2017 Mapzen copyright, and links to both upstream licenses in About. No map glyph or font files are bundled. Native safe-area positioning still needs visual acceptance. A complete transitive software-license inventory for final APK, AppImage and Flatpak artifacts remains required before publication.

description: The web, desktop, Android launcher, and Android sharing notification shall use one recognizable Constellation star in the Taskyon palette rather than generated framework placeholder icons.
notes: Generated launcher assets and a monochrome notification glyph compile in the x86_64 APK. Visual checks on installed Android and desktop launchers are still pending.

description: The app shall keep a bounded in-memory FIFO of useful map, connection, and sharing events, show redacted actual map errors, mirror safe events to the development console, and offer Copy logs from the icon menu without a log viewer.
notes: The UI session FIFO holds at most 2000 entries; repeated errors coalesce. Clipboard export is chronological and contains only sanitized details. Development console mirroring is on by default; production retains an in-memory copy action. The buffer resets on UI reload and does not collect Android service events while the UI is closed. Native acceptance of clipboard behavior remains pending.

description: First-run map guidance, the primary sharing control, sharing settings, and About shall explain decentralized end-to-end encrypted peer communication, lack of central location history, and the limits of relay, map-host, endpoint, and recipient privacy without absolute security promises.
source: Constellation product decisions;libp2p circuit relay documentation
notes: A dismissible first-run note persists its seen flag locally. The split share action and dialog state P2P encryption; the preview card and About explain immediate connection presence and optional saving. About also covers relayed ciphertext, connection metadata, map requests, local protected state, browser code trust, recipients, and approximation limits. This is explanatory product copy, not an audited security guarantee or complete legal privacy policy. Android visual acceptance remains pending.
